_why: Gzipped transfer ceilings per game. The mission is that these games are reachable on metered data, so bytes need something that refuses them. Ceilings are measured-today plus ~8% headroom, deliberately not an aspiration: a budget nobody can meet gets raised until it means nothing.
_knownWins: DONE: audio was WAV (uncompressed PCM) at 855-1270 KB gzipped per game, larger than the Phaser engine. Re-encoded to Ogg/Opus with an AAC/m4a fallback: 4352 KB of WAV across the games became 775 KB of Opus or 862 KB of AAC, and a browser downloads only one of the pair. One file per game was nearly all of it - whiteout's music_loop.wav alone was 1,176,044 bytes.

OPEN: Korean webfonts are unevenly subset. whiteout ships NanumGothicCoding at 76 KB for two weights; lastwar ships NotoSansKR at 545 KB and champs 1.09 MB across two weights, both named .subset but evidently not subset to the glyphs used. whiteout proves ~40 KB per weight is achievable for the same job.
OPEN: champs PRELOADS its two 540 KB Korean fonts from index.html, so they are part of the first wait rather than a background cost. Its cold load is 1226 KB against 366-395 KB for the other four.
_audioNote: The audio figure counts BOTH shipped formats, so it OVERSTATES what a player pays by roughly half. That is deliberate: a ceiling that over-counts fails safe, where one that guessed which format a player gets could pass a real regression.
